correctness.rationale: For 0 in Y and Y+{0,v}=T, every admissible y is in T with y+v also in T. Associate y with the edge joining these two points. The graph on T of all such edges is a disjoint union of paths: every vertex has at most one predecessor and successor, and v nonzero excludes cycles. Exact coverage is precisely an edge cover. The vertex 0 has no predecessor in the nonnegative orthant, so its edge must be chosen and the origin condition is automatic (or the fiber is empty if it is isolated). For a run of length ell the endpoint edges are forced and no two omitted edges may be adjacent. With r chosen edges the ell-1-r omissions occupy distinct gaps among the r-1 interior gaps, giving the stated binomial, including the forced single edge at ell=2. Runs are independent and singleton runs yield zero, including |T|=1. Joining any two runs by an unused bridge gives a rank-preserving injection into the covers of the longer path. A disconnected nonzero fiber with s runs has maximal degree t-s rather than t-1, proving strict inequality of the polynomials and of their evaluations at 1. The single path must start at 0, and counting binary interiors with no consecutive omissions gives F_{t-1}, including t=2. The first paragraph's 'simultaneously' is interpreted as the later explicit polynomial equality criterion, not separate rank-by-rank uniqueness: for v=1, T={0,1,3,4} has z^2 and ties h_4=z^2+z^3 at rank 2.
residual_risks: The finite census only corroborates those windows. The exact theorem is for nonzero nonnegative v, finite targets in the nonnegative lattice and the unique target attaining all coefficients simultaneously; individual ranks can tie.
